items.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: my first big break... was a band called Charlie Ventura... well, then my first big break with something that really was making a little bit of noise was a band called Charlie Ventura... since this was the first band that I was with that had a real name thing

ctx.x: Take us up into where you moved from the Grade Z...

Well they weren’t really Grade Z, I’d say about K or L. And well, then my first big break with something that really was making a little bit of noise was a band called Charlie © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

Ventura which was not a big band, it was one of those sort of ninettes, or whatever you call it. He had a four horn front line and three rhythm — I guess maybe we were seven. He at that time just after I joined him, within a year or two, I don’t know if you can remember a few years back, but you remember when Chick Corea was really at the very peak of his popularity? I think you could at that time say he was the number one small group, wouldn’t you say he had a period like that? For two or three years I mean,…

items.title: Ed Shaughnessy Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 25, 1998 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...the things I didn't know you did, with Charlie Ventura? [INTERVIEWEE] Yeah, that was my first national exposure.

ctx.x: Absolutely. And he still sounds good, too.

Oh he sounds wonderful. He sounds just great. By the way, the Charlie Ventura stuff has been reissued on CD. It’s never been on CD, you either had the big twelve inch LP’s or © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -5-
you didn’t have it, and it just came out. And I talked to a guy, do you know who Gene Norman is?
